messages:
alex-support: FYI raised from a user — their promo code is being rejected as "expired" via the API but the dashboard shows the code active. Customer email: j****@example.com, promo: SPRINGLAUNCH23, sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d

jordan-support: thanks — can you drop the exact API response body and timestamp when they tried? also which SDK/platform (web/ios/android)

alex-support: they hit it from our web checkout at 2025-03-04T18:12:22Z. API responded 400 with body: ```json
{
  "error": "promo_code_invalid",
  "detail": "code expired"
}
```

oliver-eng: pinging in. two quick checks: 1) confirm the promo entry in promo DB (id or code) and 2) share the raw redemption request headers (x-request-id, x-region) if possible

alex-support: promo id from dashboard: promo_78X, I attached screenshots in the support ticket and pasted request headers below: `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d`, `x-region: us-west-2`

oliver-eng: ok grabbing logs... small heads-up: we recently ran a CSV import for partner promos last week. there was an edge case with epoch fields. reproducing locally with their request...

oliver-eng: pasted reproduction curl (for ops/qa): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/redeem 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d" 
  -d '{"code":"SPRINGLAUNCH23","customer_email":"j****@example.com"}'
```

oliver-eng: response in our logs matches the user: ```json
{
  "error": "promo_code_invalid",
  "message": "code expired",
  "promo_check": { "starts_at": 1690000000000, "ends_at": 1710000000 }
}
```

jordan-support: whoa `starts_at` looks very large (ms) vs `ends_at` looks like seconds. that mismatch would confuse our time checks

oliver-eng: exactly. the redemption code path does these checks (pseudocode): ```js
if (now < promo.starts_at || now > promo.ends_at) throw Error('promo_code_invalid')
```
But if starts_at was imported in milliseconds (1.69e12) and ends_at in seconds (1.71e9) that makes starts_at >> now and it appears not-yet-active or immediately expired depending on branch.

hazel-ops: confirming — the partner CSV had `starts_at` in ms and we stored it verbatim. our promo table has mixed epoch units for a small subset (~82 rows).

oliver-eng: proposed mitigation: 1) quick reconciliation script to normalize epoch columns (if starts_at > 1e12 then divide by 1000) 2) update redemption logic to accept either seconds or milliseconds (backstop) 3) a small backfill to re-evaluate currently failing promo rows and mark them active if appropriate

hazel-ops: I can run the reconciliation as a one-off. steps I'll take: snapshot promo table, run the normalizer in a transaction, reindex, then re-run the failing redemption for the example. planning to run at 2025-03-04T19:00Z. will report job id

oliver-eng: thanks — can we also add a short alert to the import job if epoch values > 1e12 so we don't reintroduce this?

hazel-ops: yep will add a healthcheck and set alert to #eng-infra if > 10 malformed rows on import

jordan-support: for the customer: I'm going to issue a manual credit now and email them the confirmation. will follow up once ops confirms reconciliation so we can close the ticket instead of leaving a workaround

promo-bot: Manual credit created: credit_42c (amount: $50) for j****@example.com by jordan-support — ticket: SUP-11321 :white_check_mark:

hazel-ops: reconciliation job complete. job_id job_20250304_01. Converted 82 rows where epoch looked like ms -> normalized to seconds. Re-ran redemption for req_0a1b2c3d and now returns 200 / `{"status":"redeemed"}` :rocket:

jordan-support: great — emailed customer and refunded manual credit (we applied manual credit as temporary; we refunded since code is valid now). Will mark as resolved and link SUP-11321 to this thread. :thumbsup:

alex-support: thanks all. recording root cause as CSV import epoch-unit mismatch and adding a short postmortem to the ticket.

oliver-eng: followups: (1) add unit test for mixed-epoch promos, (2) add migration that tolerates both units on read, (3) patch import pipeline to normalize and validate. I'll open PRs this afternoon. :eyes:
